title: Vendor SLA & Liability Playbook (personal scratchpad)
content:
Purpose:
Quick personal scratchpad for negotiating vendor contracts and redlining clauses I see repeatedly. This lives in users so it's messy — notes to self, questions for Legal, negotiation scripts, and proposed one-line replacements for problematic clauses.

Top negotiation priorities (order):
1) CAP AND EXCLUSIONS: set total liability cap to (a) fees paid in prior 12 months OR (b) a fixed dollar cap tied to the contract value for the term. Prefer mutual cap.
2) INDEMNITY SCOPE: narrow to IP infringement only; avoid open-ended third-party claims for data or business losses. If asked for broader indemnity, push for mutual indemnity and carve-outs for Open Source + data processing.
3) DATA & SECURITY: require SOC2 or equivalent, timely breach notice (<72 hrs), defined data breach remediation obligations, KMS/HSM controls for keys, and no right to use customer data for model training without explicit consent.
4) SLA / CREDITS: guarantee clear SLOs (p99 latency, availability %), measurable metrics, and reasonable service credits (not termination right unless severe repeated misses). Avoid unlimited termination for small misses.
5) TERMINATION & EXIT: ensure transition assistance for 90 days, data return/secure delete, and escrow arrangements if access to critical code or models is required.
6) LIMITATION OF DAMAGES: no consequential, indirect, or lost profits damages; carve-out for gross negligence/willful misconduct.
7) GOVERNING LAW & JURISDICTION: prefer CA or NY; push back on vendor-only foreign fora.
8) ASSIGNMENT / CHANGE OF CONTROL: require notice + ability to terminate for material change in control.
9) EXPORT / COMPLIANCE: vendor must comply with export controls, sanctions lists, and provide assurance on restricted country access.
10) AUDIT RIGHTS: limit to reasonable frequency, scoped, and subject to confidentiality; avoid on-site audits without cause.

Clauses that often cause trouble (red-flag checklist):
- Broad unlimited indemnity for customer data uses
- Liability cap absent or set to ‚indemnity for direct damages only' (too vague)
- Vendor claiming rights to use customer data for training models
- Broad license-back language that assigns improvements to vendor
- Auto-renewal with short notice windows and non-cancellable long terms
- Broad confidentiality exceptions (e.g., marketing/publications)
- Termination only for material breach but with no cure period
- No SLA metrics or the metrics are unmeasurable (e.g., 'best efforts')

Quick negotiation scripts (what to say on calls / Slack):
- When they insist on broad IP indemnity: "We can meet you on IP claims tied to the services, but we can't accept open-ended liability for downstream business loss. Let's narrow to classic IP claims and agree mutual indemnity elsewhere."
- When vendor wants training rights: "We're open to limited uses for model improvement, but only on anonymized, aggregated data and under a separate data processing addendum — not a blanket grant."
- On SLA credits ask: "We need objective, auditable metrics and service credits that provide real remediation. Can you propose an outage ladder (e.g., credits at 99.9, 99.5 etc.)?"
- On audit requests: "We can agree to annual audits by a third-party auditor and reasonable advance notice — full on-site audits only for material concerns."

Suggested redline snippets (pick/adapt):
- Liability Cap: "Each party's aggregate liability for direct damages arising out of this Agreement shall not exceed the total fees paid or payable by Customer to Vendor under this Agreement in the 12 months preceding the event giving rise to the claim."
- Exclusion of Consequential: "In no event shall either party be liable for indirect, special, incidental, consequential, punitive or exemplary damages, including loss of profits, loss of data or loss of business opportunity, except to the extent such damages result from gross negligence or willful misconduct."
- IP Indemnity (narrow): "Vendor shall defend Customer against any third-party claim that the Services, as delivered by Vendor, infringe any issued U.S. patent or copyright, and shall indemnify for damages finally awarded. Vendor will have no obligation for claims arising from Customer modifications, combinations, or use outside the license scope."
- Data Use Restriction: "Vendor shall not use Customer Data to train, fine-tune, or otherwise improve any machine learning models without Customer's prior written consent. Any permitted use shall be on aggregated, anonymized data only and subject to the Data Processing Addendum."
- Termination Assistance: "Upon termination, Vendor will provide reasonable transition assistance for up to 90 days, including export of Customer Data in a common format and secure deletion of Customer Data from Vendor systems, at Vendor's expense."

Fallback concessions (what we can give):
- Mutual indemnity instead of unilateral, with robust limits and prompt notice/collaboration terms.
- Extend the liability cap for IP indemnity only (e.g., a 2x multiplier) if vendor refuses a fixed cap.
- Accept certain training-use language if anonymization + narrow data subset + revenue share or opt-out is allowed.
- Agree to longer auto-renew if we get shorter minimum term or early termination rights.

Open items for Legal / questions to escalate: (put in JIRA if needed)
- Is 12-month fees cap standard enough for deals >$5M? (LEGAL-4021)
- Acceptable language for SOC2 certificate and reporting frequency?
- Does Redwood want any special carve-outs for model outputs (regulatory/compliance exposures)?
- Precedent for escrow of model weights or critical inference code? Cost estimates?

Practical negotiation checklist (one-pager for calls):
- Start by asking for their standard SLA + cap.
- If no cap, ask for a numeric cap tied to fees. Get their justification.
- Push to narrow indemnity to IP only. Ask for mutuality.
- Confirm data use: no training without consent.
- Lock in breach notice timing and remediation obligations.
- Get measurable SLO definitions (metrics, measurement window, monitoring tool).
- If they insist on audits, limit to annual third-party audit and confidentiality controls.
- Get exit assistance and data return/secure delete spelled out.

Notes to self / negotiation memory log (example entries):
- 2026-02-12: Vendor X proposed unlimited indemnity for data: countered with IP-only + SOC2 + DPA. They balked on data training clause. Need Eng input on what can realistically be anonymized.
- 2026-02-20: Legal suggested liability cap = 12 months of fees for pilot deals; consider higher cap for strategic partnerships.
- 2026-03-05: Product asked if SLA p99 delta can be 200ms — verify with infra if realistic before agreeing.

Useful links / templates:
- Confluence: standard SLA templates (linked above)
- Last similar redline: /shared_drives/legal/redlines/vendor-redline-acme-2025.docx (ask Legal to pull)
- Slack: #legal-contracts history (search "training rights")

End of scratchpad. Will prune into a formal checklist when next negotiating. Keep this messy — it's a living doc.

Questions I still have (personal):
- Should we ever accept vendor training rights if there is a DPA + opt-out + revenue share? (short answer: maybe for low-sensitivity telemetry but not customer PII)
- Is model escrow a thing we can push for without scaring vendors away? Ask Legal for precedent and cost.
- How often do we accept a 24-month auto-renewal with 60-day cancellation window vs. prefer 12-month?
